_about: Hand-curated wars fought 1789-1815 (before Correlates of War coverage begins in 1816), for GTNW. Compiled from standard references (see SOURCES.md): Clodfelter, Warfare and Armed Conflicts (4th ed., 2017); Wikipedia 'List of wars: 1700-1799' / 'List of wars: 1800-1849' and the per-war articles named in each record's 'ref'. Dates are given to the day only where the date is a well-documented event (declaration, treaty, battle); otherwise to the month (YYYY-MM) or year. battle_deaths is filled only where a commonly cited approximate figure exists and is always flagged deaths_approx=true; otherwise null with a note. Sides use GTNW ids (DEU = Prussia/German states, AUT = Habsburg Austria, TUR = Ottoman Empire, ITA = Italian states, RUS = Russian Empire). Wars that continue past 1815 are recorded whole here; where COW also records a post-1816 phase, 'related' names that COW record.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1787-1792)
wars.terms: Treaty of Jassy: Ottomans recognise the annexation of Crimea and cede Yedisan (Ochakov) up to the Dniester.
wars.notes: Ottoman declaration of war August 1787. Austria fought alongside Russia 1788-1791 (separate record).

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1788-1791)
wars.terms: Treaty of Sistova: Austria returns Belgrade and most conquests; small gain at Old Orsova.
wars.notes: Heavy Austrian losses to disease in 1788.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1788-1790)
wars.terms: Treaty of Varala: status quo ante bellum.
wars.notes: Hostilities began June/July 1788. Denmark-Norway (Russia's ally) invaded Sweden Sep-Nov 1788 (the 'Theatre War').

wars.name: Northwest Indian War
wars.terms: Treaty of Greenville: most of present-day Ohio ceded to the United States.
wars.notes: Start conventionally 1785/1786; St. Clair's defeat (1791) and Fallen Timbers (1794).

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War
wars.terms: Treaty of Seringapatam: Tipu Sultan cedes about half of Mysore's territory to the East India Company and its allies (Marathas, Hyderabad).
wars.notes: Tipu attacked Travancore (a Company ally) Dec 1789.

wars.name: Haitian Revolution
wars.terms: Independence of Haiti proclaimed 1 Jan 1804; slavery abolished.
wars.notes: Britain (1793-1798) and Spain (1793-1795) also intervened. The 1802-1803 Leclerc/Rochambeau expedition lost roughly 50,000 men, mostly to yellow fever. Total deaths uncertain.

wars.name: War of the First Coalition
wars.terms: Peace of Basel (1795) takes Prussia and Spain out; Treaty of Campo Formio: Austria cedes the Austrian Netherlands (Belgium) to France and recognises the Cisalpine Republic, receives Venice. Britain fights on.
wars.notes: France declared war on Austria 20 Apr 1792. Prussia left Apr 1795, Spain Jul 1795; the Dutch Republic became the French-aligned Batavian Republic in 1795. ITA here = Sardinia-Piedmont and Naples.
wars.ref: Wikipedia: War of the First Coalition

wars.name: Polish-Russian War of 1792
wars.terms: King Stanislaw joins the Targowica Confederation; Constitution of 3 May annulled; Second Partition of Poland (1793) by Russia and Prussia.
wars.notes: POL = Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (GTNW's POL land; not on the board 1795-1918).

wars.name: War in the Vendee
wars.terms: Royalist armies destroyed; Charette executed March 1796; later Chouannerie flare-ups.
wars.notes: Total deaths including civilians are often put at about 170,000 (Hussenet 2007) but estimates range widely; not a battle-death count.

wars.name: Kosciuszko Uprising
wars.terms: Third Partition of Poland (1795) among Russia, Prussia and Austria; the Commonwealth ceases to exist.
wars.notes: Coded interstate because the Commonwealth's government joined the rising; some references treat it as an uprising.

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1796-1802)
wars.terms: Peace of Amiens: Spain cedes Trinidad to Britain; Minorca returned to Spain.
wars.notes: Spain allied with France by the Treaty of San Ildefonso (1796).

wars.name: Irish Rebellion of 1798
wars.terms: Rebellion crushed; led to the Act of Union 1800 (United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, 1 Jan 1801).
wars.notes: French expedition landed at Killala Aug 1798. Deaths commonly estimated at 10,000-30,000 including civilians.

wars.name: Quasi-War
wars.terms: Convention of 1800 (Mortefontaine): ends the 1778 Franco-American alliance; no reparations.
wars.notes: Undeclared naval war; deaths well under 1,000 (below the COW war threshold).

wars.name: French campaign in Egypt and Syria
wars.terms: French army capitulates at Alexandria; Egypt restored to Ottoman rule.
wars.notes: Part of the War of the Second Coalition. Mamluk forces fought on the Ottoman side.
wars.ref: Wikipedia: French invasion of Egypt and Syria

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition
wars.terms: Treaty of Luneville (1801): Austria confirms Campo Formio, left bank of the Rhine to France. Peace of Amiens (1802): Britain returns most conquests except Trinidad and Ceylon.
wars.notes: Naples (ITA) attacked the Roman Republic in Nov 1798; France declared war on Austria in Mar 1799. Russia left in 1800.
wars.ref: Wikipedia: War of the Second Coalition

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.terms: Seringapatam stormed, Tipu Sultan killed; Wodeyar dynasty restored as a Company client; territory partitioned.

wars.name: War of the Oranges
wars.terms: Treaty of Badajoz: Olivenza ceded to Spain; Portugal closes its ports to British shipping.
wars.notes: Very short, low-casualty war.

wars.name: First Barbary War
wars.terms: Treaty with Tripoli: prisoners of the USS Philadelphia ransomed for $60,000; tribute ends.
wars.notes: Tripoli (an Ottoman regency, GTNW land LBY) declared war on the U.S. Sweden fought Tripoli 1800-1802. Low casualties.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.terms: Treaties of Deogaon and Surji-Anjangaon: Company gains Delhi, Agra, the Orissa coast and much of the Doab.
wars.notes: Assaye (Sep 1803), Laswari (Nov 1803).

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.terms: Treaty of Pressburg: Austria cedes Venetia to the Kingdom of Italy and Tyrol to Bavaria; Holy Roman Empire dissolved 1806. Trafalgar (Oct 1805) gives Britain naval supremacy.
wars.notes: Dated from Britain's declaration of war on France (May 1803); the continental war ran Aug-Dec 1805 (Ulm, Austerlitz). Bavaria (DEU land) fought for France; ITA = Naples (Coalition).
wars.ref: Wikipedia: War of the Third Coalition; Napoleonic Wars

wars.name: First Serbian Uprising
wars.terms: Ottoman reconquest of the Belgrade Pashalik; Karadjordje flees to Austria.
wars.notes: Russia supported the rebels during the 1806-1812 Russo-Turkish War.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1804-1813)
wars.terms: Treaty of Gulistan: Persia cedes Dagestan, eastern Georgia and most of present-day Azerbaijan to Russia.

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1804-1808)
wars.terms: Ended when the Spanish rising against Napoleon (1808) brought Spain into alliance with Britain; British invasions of the Rio de la Plata (1806-07) repulsed.
wars.notes: Overlaps the Third Coalition and the start of the Peninsular War.

wars.name: War of the Fourth Coalition
wars.terms: Treaties of Tilsit: Prussia loses about half its territory (Duchy of Warsaw and Kingdom of Westphalia created); Russia joins the Continental System.
wars.notes: Prussia's ultimatum led to war in Oct 1806 (Jena-Auerstedt 14 Oct); Eylau and Friedland 1807.
wars.ref: Wikipedia: War of the Fourth Coalition

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.terms: Treaty of Bucharest: Bessarabia ceded to Russia; Serbian autonomy promised.
wars.notes: Russian troops entered the Danubian Principalities in late 1806; the Porte declared war in Dec 1806.

wars.name: Anglo-Turkish War (1807-1809)
wars.terms: Treaty of the Dardanelles; the British Alexandria expedition (1807) had withdrawn.
wars.notes: Small war: Dardanelles operation and the failed Alexandria expedition.

wars.name: Gunboat War (Anglo-Danish War)
wars.terms: Treaty of Kiel: Denmark cedes Norway to Sweden and Heligoland to Britain.
wars.notes: Began with the British attack on Copenhagen (bombardment 2-5 Sep 1807) and seizure of the Danish fleet.
wars.ref: Wikipedia: Gunboat War; Treaty of Kiel

wars.name: Finnish War (Russo-Swedish War 1808-1809)
wars.terms: Treaty of Fredrikshamn: Sweden cedes Finland and the Aland Islands to Russia (Grand Duchy of Finland).

wars.name: Dano-Swedish War (1808-1809)
wars.terms: Treaty of Jonkoping: status quo ante bellum.

wars.name: Peninsular War
wars.terms: French driven from Iberia; Treaty of Valencay (Dec 1813) restores Ferdinand VII.
wars.notes: Portugal had been invaded in Nov 1807; the war is dated here from the Madrid rising (Dos de Mayo). Large guerrilla and civilian losses; military deaths on all sides are commonly put in the hundreds of thousands, figures vary widely.

wars.name: War of the Fifth Coalition
wars.terms: Treaty of Schonbrunn: Austria cedes Salzburg, the Illyrian Provinces and western Galicia; joins the Continental System.
wars.notes: Aspern-Essling and Wagram. Bavaria, Saxony and the Duchy of Warsaw fought for France; the Tyrolean Rebellion ran alongside.
wars.ref: Wikipedia: War of the Fifth Coalition

wars.name: Spanish American wars of independence (South America)
wars.terms: Independence of Gran Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, the United Provinces of the Rio de la Plata and Paraguay; last royalist garrison (Callao) surrenders Jan 1826.
wars.notes: Umbrella record from the 1809 juntas (Chuquisaca, La Paz, Quito) to Callao; many theatres. COW records post-1816 phases separately, so this overlaps those records.
wars.related: COW-extra 'Liberation of Chile', 'First Bolivar Expedition', 'Second Bolivar Expedition', 'Liberation of Peru'
wars.ref: Wikipedia: Spanish American wars of independence

wars.name: Mexican War of Independence
wars.terms: Treaty of Cordoba: independence of Mexico (First Mexican Empire).
wars.notes: From Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores. COW records a 1817-1818 phase separately.

wars.name: Ottoman-Wahhabi War
wars.terms: Diriyah taken and destroyed; the First Saudi State ends.
wars.notes: Fought for the Porte by Muhammad Ali's Egypt (GTNW land EGY, then Ottoman). COW records the 1816-1818 phase.

wars.name: War of 1812
wars.terms: Treaty of Ghent (signed 24 Dec 1814, ratified 17 Feb 1815): status quo ante bellum.
wars.notes: Combat deaths: U.S. about 2,260 killed in action, British/Canadian roughly 1,200-1,600; deaths from disease were several times higher. Tecumseh's confederacy fought with Britain.

wars.name: French invasion of Russia
wars.terms: Grande Armee destroyed; Prussia (Dec 1812, Tauroggen) and later Austria change sides.
wars.notes: Military deaths from all causes: Grande Armee roughly 300,000-400,000 dead, Russian army roughly 150,000-210,000; value is a midpoint, not a pure battle-death count.
wars.ref: Wikipedia: French invasion of Russia; Clodfelter (2017)

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.terms: Napoleon abdicates and is exiled to Elba; First Treaty of Paris returns France to its 1792 borders.
wars.notes: Austria joined Aug 1813; Leipzig (Oct 1813) alone cost roughly 90,000 killed and wounded. Saxony fought for France until Leipzig. ITA = Kingdom of Italy (Naples changed sides Jan 1814).
wars.ref: Wikipedia: War of the Sixth Coalition

wars.name: Creek War
wars.terms: Treaty of Fort Jackson: the Creek Nation cedes about 23 million acres in Alabama and Georgia.
wars.notes: Horseshoe Bend (Mar 1814). Overlaps the War of 1812.

wars.name: Swedish-Norwegian War (1814)
wars.terms: Convention of Moss: Norway enters a personal union with Sweden but keeps its constitution.
wars.notes: Short, low-casualty war.

wars.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
wars.terms: Treaty of Sugauli: Nepal cedes Sikkim, Kumaon, Garhwal and most of the Terai.
wars.notes: Nepal was an independent kingdom; coded colonial as an East India Company war of expansion.

wars.name: Neapolitan War
wars.terms: Treaty of Casalanza: Murat deposed; Bourbon Ferdinand restored in Naples.
wars.notes: ITA = Murat's Kingdom of Naples.

wars.name: War of the Seventh Coalition (Hundred Days)
wars.terms: Napoleon defeated at Waterloo and exiled to St Helena; Second Treaty of Paris (Nov 1815): France loses further border territory, pays 700 million francs indemnity, occupied for up to five years.
wars.notes: Dated from Napoleon's return to Paris to Louis XVIII's return. Waterloo: roughly 50,000+ killed and wounded on both sides.

wars.name: Second Serbian Uprising
wars.terms: Serbia gains autonomy under Milos Obrenovic (Principality of Serbia, 1817; formalised 1830).
wars.notes: Fighting largely over by late 1815; settlement by 1817.

wars.name: Second Barbary War
wars.terms: Treaty with Algiers: tribute and ransom payments by the U.S. end; captives released.
wars.notes: Decatur's squadron; very few deaths. The 1816 Anglo-Dutch bombardment of Algiers is in COW extra-state.
